thread:
maya: Quick one — curl API calls are failing for a customer. Their API_KEY has ampersand & and double quotes in it. When they run:
```
curl -u "$API_KEY:" https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate
```
shell splits it or curl complains about auth. Any quick tips?

sam: Try building the header explicitly and avoid letting the shell parse it. E.g. in bash:
```
export API_KEY='abc&"def$ghi'
HEADER=$(printf '%s:' "$API_KEY" | base64 | tr -d '\n')
curl -H "Authorization: Basic $HEADER" https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate
```
That avoids `curl -u` escaping issues and problems from shell metacharacters.

zack: Note: `curl -u` will base64-encode for you, but it still goes through the shell, so quoting matters. If the key has embedded newlines or CRLF from Windows editors, `-u` can still end up malformed.

ryan: Also check for trailing newline from .env or editor. Quick check:
```
printf '%s' "$API_KEY" | od -An -t x1
```
If you see `0a` or `0d` strip them:
```
export API_KEY="$(printf '%s' "$API_KEY" | tr -d '\r\n')"
```

maya: Good tip. How about Windows / PowerShell?

sam: PowerShell example:
```powershell
$raw = "$env:API_KEY" + ':'
$bytes = [System.Text.Encoding]::UTF8.GetBytes($raw)
$base64 = [System.Convert]::ToBase64String($bytes)
Invoke-RestMethod -Uri 'https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate' -Headers @{ Authorization = "Basic $base64" }
```

zack: Node / Deno example:
```js
const header = 'Basic ' + Buffer.from(`${process.env.API_KEY}:`).toString('base64')
await fetch(url, { headers: { Authorization: header } })
```

maya: Also noticed streaming client started and then got a 401 mid-stream — could that be header related? :thinking:

sam: Yes, if the header contains a stray newline or the base64 tool inserted a linebreak, auth will fail after the initial handshake. Use `tr -d '\n'` or `base64 -w0` (GNU) to prevent wrapping.

maya: Thanks all :thumbsup: I'll paste this back to the customer and try the `tr -d` trick.
